S1 — WHOLE-INPUT APOSTROPHE CHOICES CANNOT COMPOSE INTERNAL JOINING AND EXTERNAL BOUNDARIES.
Locations: packages/core/src/discovery/signals.ts:145, :177-181, :209-220. The two input variants treat every apostrophe identically for the entire input: join all or split all. Names require joined internal apostrophes, while possessive/quote boundaries sometimes require splitting. Neither variant can represent both in one mention. This is the surviving .8 S1, independently confirmed and broadened to name-reason loss despite alias rescue.
Concrete input "Land's Stride's effect": expected U("land's stride") = [feature:circle-of-the-land:lands-stride, feature:ranger:lands-stride]; actual name keys [], ambiguity [], candidates [], retained packet []; each expected key must have the other as its sibling. Joined input is "lands strides effect"; split input is "land s stride s effect"; indexed name is "lands stride". Actual rendered packet retained nothing. "before'Land's Stride" and "Land's Stride'after" also fail; all 0027/2018/2019 internal/external combinations fail the same class.
Concrete input "Hunter's Mark's damage": expected [spell:hunters-mark], siblings []; actual [subclass:hunter], no spell name reason. The shorter Hunter match is an independent legitimate match; suppressing it is not the repair.
Exact sibling membership: 47 of all 2,009 n+"'s effect" inputs lose expected canonical keys, union 45 keys. Raw-name reasons are lost for 58 inputs; e.g. alchemist's fire's effect can retain equipment:alchemists-fire-flask through plural alias "alchemist's fires", while its "alchemist's fire" reason is lost. On 63 apostrophe-bearing forms, the 1,701 FULL-stack mixed-grammar cases lose keys in 1,476 cases / lose exact-name reasons in 1,575 cases, 59 forms / the same 45 keys. All five affected kinds are equipment, feature, hazard, rule and spell. The exact 45-key population is the UNION of U(n) minus emittedNameKeys(extract(n+"'s effect", FULL stack)); the 59-form mixed population is the union of failed key/reason cases in the explicit 3x3x3 grammar above. This deterministic query enumerates the whole class; not just the examples.
Additional state/consumer evidence: putting feature:ranger:lands-stride into stateFields.selected restores only direct-state-ref for that key (and its typed grantor relationship); it does not emit a Land's Stride name reason or restore the circle-of-the-land sibling. Plain Land's Stride surfaces both, with correct per-name siblings through packet/projection. Name/index order does not repair S1.
Permanent-evidence gap: test/discovery/nameMentionReasons.test.ts:226-231 has no mixed apostrophe role. Its :224-225 claim that batching cannot mask a miss is false for key-only expectations when several aliases share a key: grouping the real apostrophe forms with the failing n+"'s effect" transform reduced full-stack missing-name-key cases from 47 isolated inputs to 36 batched cases; eleven plural forms were masked by other aliases (alchemist's fires and ten pack/kit plurals). Assert per-name/key REASONS or isolate mentions; key presence alone is insufficient.
Required closure: independently handle joining apostrophes and external boundaries locally, keeping every recognized raw indexed-name reason with its own U(n)-minus-k siblings, one signal per key and unchanged retention/ranking. Generalized grammar evidence over real apostrophe-bearing index forms, including mixed internal/external glyphs and alias rescue, is proportionate to losing named governing material.

S2 — POSSESSIVE 's LEAVES AN EXTRA TOKEN INSIDE A MULTI-WORD NAME.
Locations: packages/core/src/discovery/signals.ts:178-181 and :209-220. There is no per-token possessive-base handling. The split variant makes 's a separate "s" token; the joining variant appends s to the previous token. When a later token still belongs to the indexed name, both violate contiguous token equality. This is independent of S1: names with NO internal apostrophe fail.
Concrete input "Shield's of Faith" (curly also): expected [spell:shield-of-faith], siblings []; actual [equipment:shield, spell:shield], no shield-of-faith signal/candidate/packet. The split variant is "shield s of faith", joined variant "shields of faith". "Death's Saving Throws": expected [rule:death-saving-throws], siblings []; actual [rule:casting-a-spell-saving-throws, rule:monsters-saving-throws, rule:saving-throws] via the shorter saving-throws name.
Ambiguous alias case "Spellcasting's Ability": expected name "spellcasting ability" keys [feature:bard:spellcasting, feature:cleric:spellcasting, feature:druid:spellcasting, feature:paladin:spellcasting, feature:ranger:spellcasting, feature:sorcerer:spellcasting, feature:warlock:pact-magic, feature:wizard:spellcasting, rule:charisma-spellcasting-ability, rule:intelligence-spellcasting-ability, rule:wisdom-spellcasting-ability]. For each key this alias requires the other TEN keys as its siblings. Actual name keys are the seven non-warlock Spellcasting feature keys plus rule:special-traits-spellcasting, rule:spellcasting and rule:spellcasting-chapter. Four expected identities are absent; all eleven alias reasons are absent. The seven surviving feature keys carry only the shorter spellcasting name and that name's DIFFERENT sibling set. Identity rescue cannot discharge the longer alias's reason.
Another colliding input "Ability's Score Improvement": expected all feature:<class>:ability-score-improvement keys for barbarian/bard/cleric/druid/fighter/monk/paladin/ranger/rogue/sorcerer/warlock/wizard (12 keys, each with the other 11 siblings); actual [].
Exact membership/state space: for each n in N WITHOUT an internal apostrophe, split at normalized spaces and independently add "'s" to each token position BEFORE the last token. FULL-stack enumeration: 2,115 cases, 2,052 with missing expected keys, union 1,220 missing keys; 1,292 raw names lose an expected name reason. This isolated population proves S2 without S1. Across all N/all 4,196 positions, 2,170 cases miss keys (same 1,220-key union) and 2,244 cases miss reasons (1,355 forms). Straight/left-curly/right-curly reproduce; trailing apostrophe alone, including natural s' on the 771 s-ending tokens, had zero reduced-index misses.
Proof gap: test/discovery/nameMentionReasons.test.ts:263-271 labels a test possessive, but checks only unrelated "hide" in "the wizard's hide", never Wizard's name signal; there is no earlier-token multi-word possessive expectation.
Required closure: grammatical possessive alternatives must be computed per input token and usable without adding a residual s token between name tokens. Preserve the observed joined spelling as well, so an intrinsic indexed apostrophe is not erased. Permanent evidence should generalize over earlier/final token positions and at least one ambiguous section alias, independently enumerating name-specific keys/reasons. The user explicitly requested this any-token dimension; it is a bounded grammatical recognition contract, not semantic paraphrase retrieval.

S3 — APOSTROPHE GLYPHS ARE NOT CANONICALIZED AT THE SHARED INDEX/INPUT BOUNDARY.
Locations: packages/core/src/rules/stack.ts:314-320 (only 2018/2019 map to 0027), :367-369 (only 0027 gets apostrophe-free indexed alias); packages/core/src/discovery/signals.ts:145/:148/:177-180; downstream rules/lookup.ts:131-132 and rules/recordRelationships.ts:508.
U+02BC MODIFIER LETTER APOSTROPHE is retained by Unicode letter matching, so it is neither joining-normalized nor a quote/possessive boundary. Fullwidth apostrophe U+FF07 and reversed single quotation U+201B instead become separators, incorrectly splitting joining spellings. The exact identical unusual glyph, if present in both an in-memory index and input, does work: the defect is the glyph-equivalence/boundary contract, not a claim that all raw Unicode names fail.
Concrete input "Landʼs Stride": expected the same two Land's Stride feature keys and mutual sibling sets; actual []. "Thievesʼ Cant": expected [feature:rogue:thieves-cant], actual []. Both kind-scoped by-name lookups return not_found instead of the indexed hit/ambiguity. "Land＇s Stride" and "Land‛s Stride" also emit no name keys, and lookup_rules' delegated lookup misses.
Boundary-only examples with an EXACT indexed name: "ʼShieldʼ" or "beforeʼShieldʼafter" expected [equipment:shield, spell:shield], mutual siblings; actual []. "Darkvisionʼs effect": expected [rule:darkvision, rule:senses-darkvision, spell:darkvision], each with the other TWO siblings; actual [].
Exact membership: replacing the 0027 in each of the 63 apostrophe-bearing forms by 02BC loses every form's expected keys, union 49 keys. These are S1's 45 keys plus creature:will-o-wisp, equipment:thieves-tools, feature:rogue:thieves-cant, spell:heroes-feast. FF07/201B internal discovery splits 59 forms, union S1's 45 keys; their four trailing-apostrophe forms happen to survive discovery. All 63 forms miss kind-scoped lookup for each of 02BC/FF07/201B (49 keys), because lookup does exact normalized-map access. For n+"ʼs effect" across ALL N, FULL stack loses keys in 1,967 inputs / reasons in 1,968, union 1,798 keys (all records except rule:what-is-a-spell). The reduced isolated-name external matrix covers all 2,009 forms/all 1,799 keys when quote-edge forms are included.
Consumer/sibling search: lookupRulesRecord, retiredNameMatch and manifest name relationships all share normalizeRulesRecordName; a discovery-only 02BC replacement would leave by-name tool queries inconsistent. The 197 presently resolved named manifest relationships do not require new aliases; repair shared character canonicalization while retaining their exact/ambiguous behavior. In-memory regenerated Land's Stride indexes with six glyph spellings confirmed that literal spelling identity is reachable, but only 0027/2018/2019 automatically produce the existing apostrophe-free name form.
Required closure: explicitly define the supported apostrophe glyph set, including required 0027/2018/2019/02BC and ordinary fullwidth/single-quote variants established for this repair; apply character equivalence consistently before index alias generation, discovery lexing and exact lookup. Do not blanket-delete Unicode modifier letters or language letters merely because their Unicode character name contains APOSTROPHE. Permanent evidence: shared supported-glyph invariant across actual byName indexing, discovery, quoted/possessive edges and exact lookup; source-distinct ambiguity and existing name reasons must survive. Other-language prime/saltillo/NKO/tag probes are inventory evidence, not an instruction to transliterate every glyph as English punctuation.
RECOMMENDED STRUCTURAL CLOSURE FOR ONE REPAIR
Replace whole-input apostrophe rewriting with a common low-level name lexer/normalizer and local, bounded grammatical matching:
1. Canonicalize the explicitly supported apostrophe characters once; share that character policy between normalizeRulesRecordName/index alias creation and discovery. Preserve current case/whitespace/dash policy and source text.
2. Lex input once, retaining apostrophe/quote positions and token offsets. Ordinary punctuation/symbols are boundaries; indexed joining apostrophes remain lexical spelling. Give each INPUT token its observed normalized spelling and justified possessive-base alternative independently (e.g. stride's can match stride; land's retains joined lands). Recognize external quote boundaries locally, including abutting text, without forcing every other apostrophe to be a boundary. Never strip arbitrary terminal s from unmarked words.
3. Tokenize indexed names with the SAME lexical definitions, retaining their actual joining spelling and raw-name identity. Compile token paths or match local token alternatives against the index. If quote/join roles need alternatives, use a local graph/trie or bounded automaton; do not enumerate 2^apostrophes whole-input rewrites. Do not create suffix-derived aliases in the index that erase an intrinsic source name.
4. Keep raw indexed-name-to-key membership explicit. After a match, union keys across all kinds for THAT name, preserve U(n)-minus-k for each name reason, collect every matching name on ONE signal per canonical key, retain stable primary-name order. A shorter independently matching name may coexist; neither rank by kind nor silently change route-count retention.
5. Keep the exact kind-scoped lookup contract distinct from player-text mention parsing: share supported character equivalence, but do not make lookup_rules silently accept arbitrary substrings or every possessive stem, nor merge away source-distinct identities because folded spellings collide.
6. Reconcile comments and canonical-discovery statusReasoning at docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json:316 with actual closure. The current claim that punctuation and possessives reach bare names is too broad in S1-S3. No pack text rewrite or new alias ontology is needed.

WHAT DISTINGUISHES CLOSED FROM UNCLOSED
Use independent grammar transformations on real index members to define expectations, rather than duplicating the production folding rule in the expected-value helper. For every transformed mention that the admitted grammar says denotes raw indexed form n, require ALL U(n) keys AND a (n,k) reason for each with EXACT U(n)-minus-k siblings. Key-only assertions miss both alias rescue and longer-name loss.

The repair is still UNCLOSED if Land's Stride's effect reaches only a state-ref, if one of its two keys disappears, if alchemist's fire survives only via alchemist's fires, if Spellcasting's Ability loses the warlock/ability-rule members or alias reason, if only U+0027 is fixed, if quoted U+02BC Shield still fails, or if a discovery-only glyph fix leaves exact lookup/index creation inconsistent.

Re-run the bounded exhaustive INDEX enumeration from the coverage table after the structural change: ordinary 2,009 names/1,799 printed titles; 63 apostrophe forms with mixed roles; all 4,196 token positions (including 771 s-ending positions); all supported glyphs; all Unicode P/S behavior classes with all indexed names; aliases and overlapping names; ordinary exact lookup and current relationship targets. Exercise actual candidate/packet/render/projection boundaries on source-backed ambiguous, longer-section-alias and spell cases, plus state-reference and reversed-index/order controls. Check one signal per key, correct individual reasons, no lost routes, truthful must-consider overflow accounting and unchanged ranking.

Permanent evidence should be GENERALIZED INVARIANTS, not a pile of individual reproducers: local joining/boundary composition, per-token possessive behavior, supported-glyph equivalence, exact per-name reason/sibling preservation, and a small vertical delivery check. Extend the existing name/stack/lookup tests. Do not blindly make the 424k-case scratch diagnostic a default gate: measure cost and retain only proportionate durable evidence. Isolate mentions or assert their name-specific reasons if batching; the observed 11 masked plural forms prove per-key batching is insufficient. The existing possessive assertion must actually check the possessively mentioned name. These evidence gaps belong to the corresponding S1-S3 closure, not a fourth product-defect finding.
